rule.written_before: any image of this run was generated; values are filled from the first batch and frozen before any acceptance decision
rule.first_batch: Candidate 1 of V1 for each of the twelve main scenes SB-P1 to SB-P6 and SB-N1 to SB-N6, generated from plan version 1 with no revision. Reserve scenes use the same frozen values.
rule.detector_score_cut: The midpoint, rounded to two decimals, between (a) the median, over the twelve first-batch images, of the best detector score for each main-element query of the image's scene (one value per query and image; the main elements are those its placement sentence names), and (b) the highest best score that any first-batch image gives to any of five decoy queries naming animals absent from every plan: a giraffe, an elephant, a zebra, a kangaroo, a camel. A query counts as found when a box scores at or above the cut.
rule.scale_cut: The median, rounded to two decimals, of the share of the frame covered by the main-element box (the smallest box enclosing the best box of each main element; for SB-N6 the two best distinct table boxes), over the first-batch images whose main elements are all found at the score cut.

fixed_constants_set_before_any_image.same_object: two boxes are the same object when intersection over union >= 0.30 or >= 70 percent of the smaller box lies inside the larger
fixed_constants_set_before_any_image.side_boundary: half the image width (centre x share 0.5): left means < 0.5, right means > 0.5
fixed_constants_set_before_any_image.record_floor: boxes scoring >= 0.05 are recorded (the best box of each query is always recorded); recording only
fixed_constants_set_before_any_image.main_element_queries: the placement sentence's subject, 'The/her' replaced by 'a/an', one query per noun joined by 'and', head noun only (an 'of ...' complement dropped: SB-N4 'a bowl'); 'The two tables': 'a table', two best distinct boxes

superseded_values.why: computed by rounding twice (areas to four decimals, then the median to two with Python round(), which returns 0.155 as 0.15)

corrections.decided_by: the coordinator, on David's study, after the run report
corrections.reason: The written rule takes the median of the first-batch main-element box areas and rounds it to two decimals. The script rounded twice: each area to four decimals (SB-P6 V1 0.15502906 -> 0.155), then the median 0.155 to two decimals with Python round(), which gives 0.15 because 0.155 is stored in binary as slightly less than 0.155.
corrections.rule: unchanged; 0.16 is the written rule applied once: the unrounded median rounded half-up to two decimals
corrections.detector_score_cut: unchanged at 0.29 (unrounded midpoint 0.287 gives 0.29 under either rounding)
corrections.consequence: Every decision that uses the scale cut was re-judged in candidate order at 0.16; see setB/README.md and manifest.csv.

amendments.name: plan-faithfulness condition
amendments.status: decided before any participant data; color sentence excluded as too vague to judge
amendments.decided_by: the coordinator, on David's study, after the plan-sentence diagnostic
amendments.reason: B1 tells participants that the image matches Alex's plan, and B2's matches/departs manipulation depends on it; the diagnostic showed content misses in SB-P2 V1, SB-P3 I2, SB-N3 V1, SB-N4 I2 and SB-N6 I2.
amendments.condition: every Set B file, V1 and I2: the description model answers yes to 'Does this photograph fit the following description: "<sentence>"?' for each of plan version 1's first three sentences (subject, arrangement, light); the fourth (colors) stays a recorded diagnostic only
amendments.how_applied: asked of every new candidate; for earlier candidates asked only where it decides (the candidate passes every other check); answers already recorded by the plan-sentence diagnostic for the same question and the same image are reused. Candidate order still decides acceptance; every accepted file was re-judged in order; the 20-try rule and the one recorded revision apply per file; no reserve swap without the orchestrator.
